newsitem.title: USA: FoxMeyer Health in talks to sell unit - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: FoxMeyer Health in talks to sell unit - WSJ.

text.p: FoxMeyer Health Corp is in talks with McKesson Corp aimed at a sale of FoxMeyer's drug-distribution unit to McKesson, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday.
The negotiations for FoxMeyer Drug Co, which filed for bankruptcy protection on August 27, have been ongoing for months, the Journal said, quoting an anonymous source.

The article said a letter filed with the Wilmington bankruptcy court reveals that the newly hired chief executive of FoxMeyer Drug, Robert Peiser, would receive $2 million if FoxMeyer Drug is acquired by McKesson within 60 days of the bankruptcy filing.
The price of the unit is not known, but a deal reached shortly before the bankruptcy filing to sell the unit - which eventually fell through - priced FoxMeyer Drug at $25 million, the article said.
Neither company was immediately available to comment on the article.
